sections.h2: What are your options for selling a house in Queen Creek, Arizona?
sections.html:
Queen Creek sellers can list with an agent, sell without one, or take an offer from a cash buyer who does not rely on a mortgage. Owner-occupied housing is the norm here, with 90.2 percent of occupied homes lived in by their owners.

  • List with an agent: the house is marketed widely, and you handle showings, buyer repair requests and the wait for loan approval.
  • Sell on your own: you price the house, deal with buyers directly and prepare the deed and affidavit of property value.
  • Cash sale: the buyer pays without a lender, and you compare the offer with the net from a listing after fees and repairs.

If an association governs your street, ask it for its governing documents and any unpaid dues before you accept an offer, since a buyer will want them at closing.

sections.h2: How big is Queen Creek and how fast has it grown?
sections.html:
Queen Creek has grown very quickly. The Census Bureau counted 26,361 residents in 2010 and 59,519 in 2020, and it estimates 89,770 as of July 1, 2025, a gain of 51.4 percent over the 2020 base. The town covers about 40 square miles of land, with 1,476 people per square mile in 2020.

The community began as a railroad flag stop named Rittenhouse, after C. H. Rittenhouse, who formed the Queen Creek Farms Company in 1919 to ship produce. The creek takes its name from the Silver Queen Mine, and the town incorporated on September 5, 1989. The old Rittenhouse Elementary School, built in 1925 and used until 1982, now houses the San Tan Historical Society museum.

Most of the town lies in Maricopa County. The eastern and southern edges reach into Pinal County, and the Ironwood Crossing neighborhood joined the town by annexation in 2018. That split matters when you sell, because the county recorder and county assessor depend on which side of the line the parcel sits.

sections.h2: Where does Queen Creek sit, and what surrounds it?
sections.html:
Queen Creek is a suburb in the far southeast of the Phoenix metro area, at an elevation of 1,417 feet. Mesa borders it to the north, Apache Junction lies to the northeast, San Tan Valley is to the east, Gilbert is on the west and the 10,200-acre San Tan Mountain Regional Park sits to the south. Queen Creek is a Valley Metro member, but the agency runs no scheduled service there and provides vanpools. The mean commute is 31.1 minutes.

That commute is longer than in Prescott (19.0 minutes), and it matters to a buyer comparing Queen Creek with homes closer to Phoenix. Be ready to answer questions about drive times to work and to the freeway when you show or describe the house.

sections.h2: How does desert heat affect a Queen Creek house?
sections.html:
Queen Creek has a hot desert climate, and heat is the main force on the house. Temperatures reach or pass 100 degrees on about 103 days a year, and 11 of those days hit 110 or more. The record high is 119 degrees, and annual precipitation is only about 8.3 inches, mostly from the July to mid-September monsoon with a lighter winter season.

These conditions shape what a buyer checks.

  • Air conditioning: a buyer will ask the age of the unit and the service history.
  • Roof and attic: sustained heat ages roofing materials and attic ventilation matters.
  • Pool equipment, if the lot has a pool: pumps and decking see heavy use during the long summers.
  • Monsoon storms: check grading and gutters, since a short, hard storm can pool water against a foundation.

Hard freezes of 28 degrees or lower happen only every couple of years, so frozen pipes are a smaller worry than in northern Arizona.

sections.h2: Which school districts serve Queen Creek homes?
sections.html:
Six public school districts serve the town, so the district depends on the address. Most of the Maricopa County part falls in Queen Creek Unified School District, with portions in Higley Unified and Chandler Unified. The Pinal County part is divided among Florence Unified, J. O. Combs Unified and Apache Junction Unified.

Schools listed for the town include Queen Creek High School, Casteel High School, Crismon High School and Newell Barney College Prep, along with several elementary and junior high schools. Charter options in town include American Leadership Academy and Benjamin Franklin Charter School. Tell buyers to confirm the assigned school for the exact address with the district, because boundaries do not follow town limits.

sections.h2: Can a buyer rent a Queen Creek house as a short-term rental?
sections.html:
Yes, but the owner must register the property with the town. Arizona law, A.R.S. 9-500.39, allows short-term rentals in all municipalities, and the Town of Queen Creek later amended its rules at a November 1 council meeting to remove the license and fees while keeping registration. The town's short-term rental page lists what an owner needs before registering.

  • Confirm the property lies inside the town limits, using the town's "Do I live in QC?" map.
  • Obtain a transaction privilege tax license from the Arizona Department of Revenue, which applies even if the owner books through an online marketplace.
  • Register the rental with the Maricopa County Assessor (602-506-3406) or Pinal County Assessor (520-866-6361) under A.R.S. 33-1902.
  • Provide the parcel number and emergency contact information.

Registration questions go to Development@QueenCreekAZ.gov. An association's rules may be stricter than the town's, so a buyer should read them first.

sections.h2: How do permits and code complaints work in Queen Creek?
sections.html:
The town runs permits, zoning, engineering, traffic applications and code enforcement complaints through its Development Nexus online portal. You can search project history for a property there, and the town's Development Nexus page lists 480-358-3003 for help. The town warns that legitimate permit payment emails come only from DevSvcsNexus@queencreekaz.gov, payment is made only through the portal by ACH or credit card, and it never asks for wire transfers.

If you built an addition, patio cover or pool, check the portal for permit records before you list. A missing final inspection is better fixed by you than discovered by a buyer's inspector.

sections.h2: What does recording a Queen Creek sale cost?
sections.html:
In Maricopa County the standard recording fee is $30 per document, and a certified copy costs $1 per page plus $3 per document certification, according to the Maricopa County Recorder fee page. For a parcel in the Pinal County part of town, ask the Pinal County Recorder for its current fee.

Each deed that transfers title must carry an affidavit signed by the buyer and seller, or their agents, under A.R.S. 11-1133, and the recorder must refuse a deed without a complete affidavit unless the deed bears an exemption notation. The affidavit asks for the price, the parcel number and whether the house will be owner-occupied or rented. Your title or escrow company usually prepares it with the deed.

faqs.q: Is Queen Creek in Maricopa County or Pinal County?
faqs.a: Both. Most of the town lies in Maricopa County, and the eastern and southern edges reach into Pinal County. The Ironwood Crossing neighborhood joined the town by annexation in 2018. Check your parcel number to find which county recorder and assessor apply.

faqs.q: Does Queen Creek require short-term rental registration?
faqs.a: Yes. The town dropped its short-term rental license and fees after a council amendment, but owners still register the property. You need a transaction privilege tax license from the Arizona Department of Revenue and the parcel number and an emergency contact. Email Development@QueenCreekAZ.gov with questions.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Maricopa County?
faqs.a: The standard recording fee is $30 per document. A copy of a recorded document costs $1 per page, and certification adds $3 per document. A deed must carry the affidavit of property value required by A.R.S. 11-1133.

faqs.q: How many people live in Queen Creek?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau estimates 89,770 residents as of July 1, 2025. The town had 59,519 people in the 2020 census and 26,361 in 2010. Median household income is $141,978 for 2020 to 2024.

faqs.q: Which school district serves my Queen Creek address?
faqs.a: It depends on the address. Most of the Maricopa County part is in Queen Creek Unified, with some areas in Higley Unified and Chandler Unified. The Pinal County part is divided among Florence, J. O. Combs and Apache Junction districts, so ask the district to confirm.
